text:
Alex: Heads-up — saw a tenant causing long-tail latencies in the continuous batcher. wondering if we should route small short requests around coalescing windows instead of preempting. anyone have quick thoughts?
Marta: Can you paste a sample trace? rough qps and p50/p99?
Alex: p50 ~ 30ms, p99 ~ 900ms for that tenant, most requests are < 64 tokens. batcher keeps waiting to coalesce and that pushes other tenants. trace: https://perf.example/trace/abc123
Jamal: sounds like classic head-of-line. options: 1) short-request fastpath 2) per-tenant deadline hints 3) soft priority decay. tradeoffs: complexity vs starvation prevention.
Kevin: i'd try a priority-decay where a tenant's priority drops if it blocks others. cheap to implement: token-budget counter + time-decay. also avoid oscillation with hysteresis.
Marta: worry about fairness: starving tenant could bounce between high/low. need metrics: blocked_time, cohorts_affected, eviction_count.
infra-bot: metric proposal logged: batcher.blocked_time, batcher.fastpath_invocations, batcher.priority_decay_events
Alex: quick experiment idea: route requests with tokens<=32 to fastpath (no coalesce), else normal. config snippet:
```
batcher:
  fastpath_max_tokens: 32
  fastpath_qps_limit: 200
  priority_decay_half_life_ms: 1500
```
Marta: +1 to starting with fastpath. then add decay if we still see tail interference.
Jamal: if we go fastpath, watch for tail amplification (more small requests could overload fastpath). need circuit-breaker.
Kevin: agree — circuit: if fastpath latency > 3x p50 for 1m, throttle. also ensure traces tag `fastpath=true`.
Alex: i'll spike this today (quick patch + telemetry), will post perf numbers. thanks all :thumbsup:
